sentence: Behind one model name, the router can hold several copies of the model, called deployments [FAILURE-034], [RSELECT-044].
This part decides what happens after a call to one deployment fails [FAILURE-021].
The router may bench that deployment for a few seconds, a pause called a cooldown, so new requests go to its other deployments [RDISP-191], [RSELECT-044].
note: Now cites the right claims. RDISP-191 gives the bench length, ending with 'The router's `cooldown_time`, which defaults to `DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_TIME_SECONDS`, 5 s'. RSELECT-044 has selection read 'the cooled-down deployment ids ... and removes deployments whose id is in that list'. The 'may' and 'a few seconds' fit a plain lead.

sentence: When the servers share a store, the others usually see the pause within about a second [FAILURE-009].
The router may then retry, and after that try backup models from a list, skipping any entry it already tried [FAILURE-103], [FAILURE-145].
If every deployment is paused and no backup model answers, the caller gets a "try again" error [FAILURE-179], [RDISP-115].
A pause shorter than one second stays on one server, so the others keep sending it traffic [FAILURE-006].
After most failed calls, the router's failure callback counts the failure and asks `set_cooldown_deployments` whether to bench the deployment [RDISP-190], [RDISP-193], [FAILURE-021].

Nine ordered checks and a lone-deployment 402 rule can stop the bench; otherwise the deployment's own allowance, the failure-rate rules or the allowed-fails counter decides [FAILURE-022]-[FAILURE-030], [FAILURE-035], [FAILURE-036], [FAILURE-042], [FAILURE-046].
A cooldown is one timed entry; with Redis and a length of at least 1 second, other servers usually see it within about 1 second [FAILURE-006], [FAILURE-009].
A retry policy sets same-group retries per error type, unless the request sets its retry count to 0 [FAILURE-103], [RDISP-138].
The fallback walk then tries the backup list in order, skipping entries already tried, until one succeeds [FAILURE-145], [FAILURE-150].
deployment: one configured copy of a model: an entry in the router's model list with a model name, its settings and an id.
note: RDEPLOY-001: `set_model_list` 'pops `model_name`, `litellm_params` and `model_info`' for each row. RDEPLOY-007 derives the id when `model_info` has none. RDEPLOY-186: 'Each `model_list` entry is stored as a plain dict'. The claims about a provider and per-deployment credentials are gone.

sentence: model group: all the deployments that share one public model name, such as gpt-4o.
cooldown: a timed bench: while it lasts, selection leaves the deployment out.
selection: the step that picks one deployment for each request and leaves out benched ones.
backup model: another model group that the fallback list names for the failed model group.
note: FAILURE-114: `get_fallback_model_group(fallbacks, model_group)` returns the chain configured for the group, by exact key, provider-prefixed or provider-stripped key, or `*`. The unsupported 'tried only after retries run out' is gone. Edge cases such as non-standard lists (RDISP-107) and same-group dict targets (FAILURE-141) are left to the body, which covers the latter.

sentence: cooldown decision: the step that runs the nine checks and the deciding rule, and writes the cooldown.
caller's own credential: a key or session that belongs to one caller rather than to the shared deployment, such as a stored key that was rejected or rate-limited.
provider-default deployment: a deployment the router lists as a provider's default; the checks never let it be benched.
cooldown time: how long a bench lasts: the deployment's own setting, else the error's retry-after header, else the router's, 5 seconds by default.
retryable status: 408, 409, 429 or any status of 500 and above; every other status counts as not retryable.
lone deployment: the only deployment of its model group, when the router has no other deployment it may use instead for that request.
per-minute counts: each server's own success and failure counts for a deployment, normally over a 60-second window from the first count.
note: The unsupported 'only the failure-rate rules use them' is gone. FAILURE-072: keys `<deployment_id>:successes` / `:fails` with 'a TTL of `60` seconds (set by the first increment and not extended)', in memory only, 'so each process counts only its own traffic'. FAILURE-073: 'normally a fixed 60-second window that starts at the first increment'.

sentence: allowance: how many failures a deployment may have before a bench.
note: The wrong 'one cooldown time' window is gone. FAILURE-049 benches 'when the new count is strictly greater than the threshold', and FAILURE-047 gives the threshold's sources. So the allowance is the number of failures tolerated before a bench.

sentence: allowed-fails policy: failure allowances per error type, set on a deployment or on the router; not the retry policy.

allowed-fails counter: a per-deployment failure count, shared through Redis when present, that normally resets a fixed time after the first failure, 5 seconds by default; retry-after headers never set that time.
note: FAILURE-049: key `deployment:<id>:allowed_fails` in the router cache, Redis included, 'the threshold applies across the whole fleet'. FAILURE-051: 'Normally the counter's window is fixed and starts at the first failure'. FAILURE-048 gives the TTL as the override, else `router.cooldown_time`, else `DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_TIME_SECONDS` (5); RSETUP-027 and CFG-013 give 5 s as the default. The override is only the deployment's `cooldown_time` (FAILURE-041), and the router path passes none (FAILURE-046), so no retry-after header reaches it.

sentence: connection-error text: the text "APIConnectionError", the name of the connection error type; an error message containing it stops the bench at the status check.
read interval: how often, at most, a server asks Redis about a bench it does not hold in its own memory; 1 second by default.
Prometheus metrics: numbers a monitoring system reads; each bench marks the deployment as out and adds one to its cooled-down count, when Prometheus is set up.
Slack alert: a chat message about a failed call, sent only when Slack alerting is set up and the request did not come through the proxy.
health mark: a health check's verdict on a deployment; separate from a bench, it counts only when health-check routing is on.
retry count: how many same-group retries a request gets; a retry skips a deployment that failed with a status that is not retryable, such as 400 or 404, if another remains.
note: Fixed. The closed list is gone and the rule now matches the claims. RDISP-148 adds the failed id when 'litellm.should_retry(status_code) is false. For example, 400, 401, 403 and 404 add the id, while 408, 409, 429 and 5xx do not', which fits the glossary's own 'retryable status' row and RDISP-156. RDISP-149 says selection 'removes the skipped ids from the candidates unless that would leave none', so 'if another remains' holds. The sentence does not claim that a 400 gets retried at all. That needs a policy count (RDISP-138, RDISP-155 check 3), and the story's policy paragraph already says so. RDISP-131 backs 'how many same-group retries'. A few call types stamp no failed id (RDISP-068, RCALL-063), which is too fine a point for a glossary row.

sentence: retry policy: retry counts per error type, router-wide or per model group.
fallback walk: the router's pass through the backup list, one entry at a time.
nested walk: a fallback walk that a backup model's own call starts, because each backup call goes through the router again with its own retries.
fallback depth: how many backup attempts deep a walk is; the maximum is checked only when a walk starts.
attempted set: the entries already tried for this request, shared by every nested walk; an entry with extra settings counts apart from the bare model name.
access and budget checks: two optional checks whoever builds the router can add, such as the proxy's check that a key may call a backup model.
fallback headers: response headers that report retries and fallbacks: x-litellm-attempted-retries, x-litellm-attempted-fallbacks and x-litellm-fallback-errors.
error-list opt-in: a request setting that adds the fallback-errors header when a backup model answers.
no-deployment error: the 429 error selection raises when no deployment is left to pick.
When default settings apply, no check stops the bench, and a deployment that is not lone fails with 429, then a bench for the cooldown time.
When default settings apply, no check stops it, and a deployment fails with 401 or 404, which is not a retryable status, then a bench at once, even for a lone deployment.

When default settings apply, no check stops it, and a deployment that is not lone fails with a 5xx, then a bench only if over half of at least 5 requests in this server's 60-second window failed, or all of at least 1000.
When default settings apply, no check stops it, and a lone deployment fails with 429, 408 or a 5xx, then a bench only if all of at least 1000 requests in that window failed.
When a 4xx other than 429, 401, 402, 404 and 408, such as 400 or 403, then the status check stops the bench, unless the deployment's own `allowed_fails_policy` has an entry for that error type.
When a lone deployment fails with 402, then no bench, unless the deployment's or the router's `allowed_fails_policy` has a matching entry.
When the deployment sets no allowance and the router sets an `allowed_fails_policy`, or an `allowed_fails` other than the global value, then the router's counter decides, lone deployments included.
When the chosen cooldown time is `0`, then no bench at all.
When every backup entry fails or gets skipped, then the caller gets the original error; a failed order-level walk surfaces its last failure instead.
Nine checks, in order, can stop a bench [FAILURE-022]-[FAILURE-030].
They stop it for an unknown deployment, a failure of the caller's own credential, a request rejected before the call, or a personal Copilot session or credential [FAILURE-022]-[FAILURE-026].
They also stop it for a zero cooldown time, cooldowns turned off, a status that needs no bench, or a provider-default deployment [FAILURE-027]-[FAILURE-030].
The failure callback skips an advisor orchestration failure, a 404 from a background poll, a 408 from the caller's own timeout and a caller-scoped OAuth failure [RDISP-190].
Otherwise it counts the failure and passes a cooldown time: the deployment's own `cooldown_time` if 0 or more, else a retry-after header of 0 or more, else the router's [RDISP-191], [RDISP-193].
The status check lets the decision go on for 429, 401, 402, 404 and 408, and for every status outside 400 to 499 [FAILURE-031].
It stops the bench for any other 4xx, such as 400 or 403 [FAILURE-031].
It also stops the bench for an empty status and for any error whose text contains `APIConnectionError`, even a 500 [FAILURE-031], [FAILURE-209].
Only an entry for that error type in the deployment's own `allowed_fails_policy` lets the decision go on anyway [FAILURE-032].
Under default settings, when no check stops it, one 401 or 404 benches a deployment at once, even a lone one [FAILURE-044].
One 429 benches it unless it is lone [FAILURE-043].
One 500 does not: a 5xx benches only when over half of at least 5 requests in this server's 60-second window failed, or all of 1000 for a lone one [FAILURE-043], [FAILURE-073].
Before any rule, a 402 on a lone deployment ends with no cooldown unless an `allowed_fails_policy` entry on the deployment or router matches it [FAILURE-035].
Otherwise configuration picks one of three rules [FAILURE-036], [FAILURE-042], [FAILURE-046]:

Deployment allowance. When the deployment's own settings define `allowed_fails` or `allowed_fails_policy`, the counter decides with its number for this error, else the router's threshold [FAILURE-036], [FAILURE-040].
A lone deployment with only a plain number and no matching per-error entry never benches here [FAILURE-039].
Failure-rate rules. Otherwise, when the router has no `allowed_fails_policy` and its `allowed_fails` is unset or equals the global value, these rules decide [FAILURE-042].
Router counter. In every other case the counter decides with the router's settings, lone deployments included [FAILURE-046].
The failure-rate rules read only this server's per-minute counts [FAILURE-045].
The counter adds one per failure under `deployment:<id>:allowed_fails`, in Redis too when present, so the fleet shares it [FAILURE-049].
When the deployment's own number applies, the key gains a suffix, the error's class name or `"generic"`, and each suffix counts separately [FAILURE-040], [FAILURE-049].

It benches once the count goes strictly above the threshold, the first value set among a deployment override, the router's per-error policy and the router's `allowed_fails` [FAILURE-047], [FAILURE-049].
When the counter resets in under 1 second, Redis keeps no count [FAILURE-048], [FAILURE-051].
note: The condition is now the counter's own reset time (FAILURE-048's TTL), not the cooldown time. FAILURE-051 (2): 'A TTL below 1 second becomes `EXPIRE <key> 0` ... which deletes the Redis counter right after its `INCR`'. FAILURE-200 says the same for a TTL of exactly 0.

sentence: A call fails: After most failures, the router counts the failure, picks a cooldown time and asks for a decision [RDISP-191], [RDISP-193]. A few kinds of failure, such as a timeout the caller set, skip all three [RDISP-190].
note: The early exits are back. RDISP-190: `deployment_callback_on_failure` 'returns `False` (no cooldown, no failure count)' for an advisor failure, a background-poll 404, 'a 408 caused by a caller-set timeout' and a caller-scoped OAuth failure. Those exits come before the RDISP-191 cooldown-time choice and the RDISP-193 count and decision, so all three are skipped.

sentence: Nine checks come first: The nine checks listed in the section above run in order, and the first that applies stops the bench [FAILURE-022]-[FAILURE-030]. The status check stops it for every 4xx except 429, 401, 402, 404 and 408, unless the deployment's own allowed-fails policy has an entry for that error type [FAILURE-029], [FAILURE-031], [FAILURE-032].
note: The override is restored. FAILURE-029: the gate stops the bench when FAILURE-031 says no cooldown 'and the deployment's own `model_info.allowed_fails_policy` has no non-null entry for the exception's type'. FAILURE-032 confirms that only this entry overrides it. FAILURE-031 gives the 4xx exceptions.

sentence: A lone 402 stops early: Before the three rules, a 402 on a lone deployment ends with no cooldown, unless the deployment's or the router's allowed-fails policy has an entry for that error [FAILURE-035].

The deployment's own numbers come first: A deployment with its own allowance gets counted with its number for this error, or with the router's number when it has none for this error [FAILURE-036], [FAILURE-040]. A lone deployment with only a plain allowance never benches this way [FAILURE-039].

Default settings use failure rates: A 429 benches unless the deployment is lone [FAILURE-043]. A status that is not retryable, such as 401 or 404, benches even a lone deployment [FAILURE-044]. Any other failure benches the deployment only when over half of at least 5 requests in this server's 60-second window failed, or all of at least 1000 for a lone one [FAILURE-043], [FAILURE-073].
note: The thresholds are restored. FAILURE-043's table: 'fail ratio `> ... 0.5` and requests `>= ... 5` and not single-deployment', or 'fail ratio this minute `== 1.0` and requests this minute `>= ... 1000`'. FAILURE-044 covers non-retryable statuses 'even on a single-deployment model group'. FAILURE-045/073 make the window this process's fixed 60 s. 'Any other failure' (429 on a lone deployment, 408, 409, 5xx) can bench only through those two rate rules.

sentence: The counter needs a strict excess: The router benches once the count goes above the allowance, so an allowance of 1 benches on the second failure, and 0 on the first [FAILURE-046], [FAILURE-047], [FAILURE-049].

One entry is the whole bench: The router writes one timed entry [FAILURE-052]. A background task then updates the Prometheus metrics when Prometheus is set up; the bench itself alerts no one [FAILURE-052], [FAILURE-056].
A bench is one timed entry holding the status, the error message with its first 50 characters kept and the rest starred, the time it started, and its length [FAILURE-002], [FAILURE-003].
When the servers share Redis, the others usually see it within about a second [FAILURE-009].
A bench under 1 second never reaches Redis, because Redis keeps whole seconds [FAILURE-006].
The entry sits under `deployment:<id>:cooldown` in a dedicated cooldown store: its own memory tier, plus Redis when the router has it [FAILURE-001], [FAILURE-006], [FAILURE-008].
It expires after the cooldown time [FAILURE-006].
A Slack alert is a separate path with its own conditions, and an alerting failure never changes the request's outcome [FAILURE-175], [FAILURE-177].
A server that lacks the entry in memory re-reads Redis at most once per read interval, 1 second by default [FAILURE-009].
A failed Redis write, including every cooldown under 1 second, gets swallowed, so that cooldown stays on this server [FAILURE-006], [FAILURE-203].
An entry stays active while its stored time plus its length lies ahead of the reader's clock, so clock skew between servers shifts the end [FAILURE-012], [FAILURE-188].
A synchronous read hit by a Redis error other than an open circuit breaker reports no cooldowns at all, and so does a failed shared batch read [FAILURE-015], [FAILURE-093].
An unhealthy health mark counts for 600 seconds by default [FAILURE-086].
The example assumes default settings, no retry-after header, no per-deployment cooldown time and Redis shared by two servers [FAILURE-009], [FAILURE-048], [RDISP-191].
0s, deployment dep-a: call fails with 429; benched for 5 seconds.
0s, selection for gpt-4o: next pick skips dep-a; dep-b serves.
1s, another server: re-reads the shared store; sees dep-a benched.
2s, deployment dep-b: call fails with 429; benched for 5 seconds.
3s, selection for gpt-4o: finds no deployment left; 429, try again in 5.
5s, deployment dep-a: cooldown time passes; serving again.
7s, deployment dep-b: cooldown time passes; serving again.
Before trying backup models, the router can retry the same model group, up to its retry count [RDISP-131].
A retry policy, when configured, sets that count per kind of error, such as rate limits or timeouts [FAILURE-099], [FAILURE-103].
A request that sets its own retry count to 0 turns the policy off; a router-wide 0 does not [RDISP-138].
The retry loop consults a policy only when the request did not set `num_retries` to `0` and a `retry_policy` or `model_group_retry_policy` exists [RDISP-138].
A group's own policy replaces the router-wide one whole [FAILURE-099], [FAILURE-100].
A 404 uses the not-found count first, when set; otherwise the lookup walks the error's class upward and takes the first count set, else the default count [FAILURE-102], [FAILURE-103].
A policy count replaces the retry count, so even a 400 or 404 retries that many times [RDISP-138].
After retries run out, the router can try the backup models on its list, one at a time and in order [FAILURE-114], [FAILURE-194].
It skips an entry it already tried for this request, and some entries it may not use [FAILURE-143], [FAILURE-145].
The first backup model that answers ends the search [FAILURE-150].
In a fallbacks list, an exact key wins, else a bare name entry, a provider-prefixed or provider-stripped key, then the catch-all "*" [FAILURE-114].
Across several lookup groups, a group's own chain beats the catch-all [FAILURE-119], [FAILURE-120].
The walk, `run_async_fallback`, re-raises the original error and tries nothing when it starts at or past `max_fallbacks` [FAILURE-138].
A target with a server-owned token-exchange field stops it with an error before any attempt [FAILURE-139].
Each target's identity enters the attempted set before its attempt; a target that is neither a name nor a mapping has none and never counts as a repeat [FAILURE-109], [FAILURE-145], [FAILURE-199].

Each attempt adds one to the depth and calls `async_function_with_fallbacks`, so the backup gets its own retries and can start a nested walk, from its own chain or the original group's [FAILURE-120], [FAILURE-147], [FAILURE-149].
A success sets `x-litellm-attempted-fallbacks` to the walk's depth and, with `include_fallback_errors`, appends the walk's error list [FAILURE-150].
A failure fires the failure event, may bench the target's deployment, and moves on [FAILURE-067], [FAILURE-151].
If nothing succeeds, the walk raises the latest error, or the original if it skipped every target, with no headers [FAILURE-152].

The cap is checked once: A walk that starts at or past the maximum depth raises the original error and tries nothing [FAILURE-138]. A walk already running never checks the maximum again [FAILURE-147].

The failed model is skipped by name: An entry that is just the failed model's name gets skipped [FAILURE-141]. An entry with extra settings, such as an order level, still runs even when it names that model [FAILURE-109], [FAILURE-141].

Some requests stay put: Some operations keep to the original model group when the request carries a file, batch or job id [FAILURE-137], [FAILURE-142]. They are creating or cancelling a batch, creating, cancelling or reading a fine-tuning job, and reading or deleting a file; creating a file also stays [FAILURE-137].

Optional access and budget checks: Whoever builds the router can add an access check and a budget check, such as the proxy's check that a key may call a backup model [FAILURE-143], [FAILURE-219]. An entry either check rejects gets skipped and recorded [FAILURE-143], [FAILURE-144].

Tried entries get skipped: The walk skips an entry already tried anywhere in this request, counting an entry with extra settings apart from the bare model name [FAILURE-109], [FAILURE-145]. An entry that is neither a model name nor a set of settings never counts as tried, so it can run again [FAILURE-109], [FAILURE-184].
note: The 'at most once' title is gone, and the exception is now stated. FAILURE-109 (4): 'any other shape has the key `None` and is never deduplicated'. FAILURE-184: such a target 'is never skipped as a repeat'. FAILURE-145 and FAILURE-111 (the set is 'shared by reference for the whole fallback walk of one request') support the first sentence.

sentence: A backup call can nest: Each backup call goes through the router again, with its own retries, and can start a nested walk of its own [FAILURE-149].
The first success ends the walk: The walk reports its depth in a header and returns, trying no later entry [FAILURE-150].
A failure moves on: The walk keeps the error and moves to the next entry [FAILURE-151].

When no deployment of a model survives selection, cooldowns included, it fails with a 429 (too many requests) error whose message starts with "No deployments available for selected model" [RSELECT-054], [FAILURE-179].
That error goes to the router's backup handling like other failures; in the usual case the caller sees it only if no backup model answers [RDISP-096], [RDISP-115].
The error is a `RouterRateLimitError`; its "Try again in" value is the smallest configured cooldown among the model's deployments [FAILURE-017], [FAILURE-178].
It adds that all deployments are in cooldown only when every deployment of the model is cooling, and its cooldown list names every benched deployment in the router [FAILURE-178], [FAILURE-179].
Under default settings, a 429 or 5xx never benches a lone deployment unless all of at least 1000 requests in a minute failed, so the router keeps sending to it [FAILURE-043].

The router compares its own failure allowance with the library-wide default, 3 unless changed; an equal value counts as unset, so a router allowance of 3 gets the failure-rate rules [FAILURE-042], [FAILURE-208]. A deployment's own allowance of 3 still counts [FAILURE-036].

With the maximum number of fallbacks set to 1 and three backup models listed, all three get tried when each fails [FAILURE-147]. The setting only stops each backup from starting fallbacks of its own [FAILURE-147].

A bench shorter than one second stays on one server, so the other servers keep sending traffic to that deployment; this matters when someone sets a cooldown time under 1 second [FAILURE-006], [FAILURE-187].
An error whose message merely contains the connection-error text stops the bench at the status check, whatever its real status code [FAILURE-031], [FAILURE-209].
A stored cooldown keeps the first 50 characters of the error text unmasked, so a key echoed early in a provider error can reach the shared store and the logs [FAILURE-210].
The "try again in" number is the shortest configured cooldown, not the time left on any cooldown [FAILURE-017], [FAILURE-178].
The x-litellm-attempted-fallbacks header can undercount: when a nested walk succeeds, each outer walk overwrites it with its own smaller depth [FAILURE-213], [FAILURE-216].
